money_at_stake.rationale: Three independently dated, officially sourced figures all land comfortably in the tens of billions and none approaches a hundred: Thailand's Board of Investment recorded 1,016,962 million baht (about USD 30.7-31.8bn) of investment-promotion applications across 624 projects in Q1 2026, of which the digital sector accounted for 873,741 million baht across 48 projects; separately, cumulative BOI-approved data-center-specific projects from 2024 to 2026 total 42 projects, 3,400 MW of combined IT load and THB 750 billion of investment; and 2025 alone saw 26 approved data-center projects worth almost THB 500 billion. Deliberately NOT a single point estimate: the Q1 2026 figure is applications rather than disbursed capital, the 2024-2026 figure is a different (narrower, DC-specific) cut, and adding them would double-count projects that appear in both. All three cuts independently clear the B1_10 floor and stay well under GT_100B, so B10_100 is the honest band regardless of which cut is used as the anchor. Note on the primary source: the candidate record's cited SCMP article (2026-08-29) could not be verified by direct fetch this run, it returned an unrelated PCB-manufacturing story rather than the data-center piece, so the underlying claim is instead independently corroborated here against three separately fetched primary reports, each re-verified against its live page on 2026-08-30.

public_reach.rationale: A genuine but partial reach, still closer to the method's 40 anchor (split with a large unlisted share) than its 60 one (clearly reachable, mixed), so scored at the midpoint of that range. On the reachable side: Gulf Development, Thailand's largest listed energy company by market value, has a dated, board-disclosed plan to raise data-center service capacity to 2,000 MW within three to five years and to invest up to 140 billion baht (about USD 4.3bn) toward it, operating through a joint venture that already runs GSA Data Center 01 in Samut Prakan; WHA Corporation (listed) is separately running a feasibility study for a dedicated data-center industrial estate needing around 1,000 MW of green power. Against it: neither of the two named listed plays accounts for more than a fraction of the tens-of-billions-baht Q1 2026 digital-sector pool the money leg cites, and Gulf's own capex figure is independently described by its CFO as a ceiling rather than a committed spend (see timing_fit). No source opened this run attributes the residual majority of that pool to any other specific listed issuer; it plausibly sits with multinational hyperscale tenants, private and PE-backed data-center operators, and state transmission spend (EGAT's capex is not an equity position at all), but this run could not independently source a breakdown of the pool by ownership type, so that residual is reasoned inference rather than a cited fact and is not weighted as heavily as it was before this pass. Correction: an earlier version of this item cited a CNBC report naming Chinese AI firms (including Moonshot AI) routing around export controls through Thailand-based data-center capacity as a further demand-side leak. That URL returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch this run and no Wayback Machine snapshot could be retrieved either, so the claim is removed rather than carried on a page that was never actually opened. The same earlier version also asserted the Gulf/WHA joint venture (GSA) included Singtel and AIS as partners; the cited Reccessary source does not contain either name anywhere in its text on re-fetch, so that detail is removed too. Scored at 50, not lower: two large, specific, listed-company plans exist and are individually well-evidenced, even though neither is a completed commitment and neither is shown to represent more than a minority of the total pool.

capture_odds.rationale: Two-sided and scored below the midpoint because a live regulatory shock is already visibly redirecting money away from the layer this occurrence's headline figures describe. For capture: the new grid-access rule functions as a qualification gate that favors incumbents with existing generation and interconnection, most visibly Gulf as the large listed IPP already selling power into this exact demand, and the new dedicated data-center electricity tariff (about 5-6 baht per kWh against a roughly 3-4 baht household rate) is a favorable, protected price band for power sellers rather than for data-center operators paying it. Against capture: those same rules, a mandatory 4.5-million-baht-per-MW financial guarantee and a requirement to prove power availability before a project can even apply for BOI promotion, have already stopped the flow this leg is trying to size. No new data-center promotion applications have been filed since April 2026, which is the same month the Q1 2026 surge was reported, so the headline pool this appraisal cites is largely money that applied and then hit a regulatory wall rather than money confirmed to convert into paid-up investment. That is closer to money getting delayed or renegotiated than money getting competed away outright, which is why this sits at 45 rather than lower. Both evidence items re-verified by direct fetch this run; unchanged from the prior version.

timing_fit.rationale: Below the method's 60 'credible inside the window' anchor, because the two concrete signals available this run cut against near-term conversion rather than for it. Gulf Development's up-to-140-billion-baht, five-year capacity plan, the single most specific listed-issuer commitment tied to this occurrence, is described by Gulf's own CFO as a ceiling rather than a committed spend, with the article's own framing that investors should watch for actual offtake commitments rather than the framework figure itself. Correction: an earlier version of this leg's evidence asserted the opposite, that this plan 'was announced as a signed strategic commitment, not a proposal,' citing the same CryptoBriefing URL. A re-fetch of that page this run found the opposite stated directly by the source, so that evidence item is deleted rather than repaired, and is replaced here with an accurately quoted item. WHA's estate is separately still at feasibility-study stage, not yet a committed capacity plan either. Meanwhile the entire new-application pipeline into the Board of Investment's data-center promotion track has been frozen since April 2026 under a rule published in the Royal Gazette on 5 June 2026 requiring sponsors to prove confirmed power availability before they can even apply, and this run could not source any confirmed date by which that freeze lifts. Correction: an earlier version of this leg's evidence additionally asserted that a fuller Energy Regulatory Commission screening framework was 'not expected to take effect until around the fourth quarter of 2026,' citing the MCG Asia article. A direct re-fetch of that page, searched specifically for 'Q4', 'fourth quarter', 'Energy Regulatory Commission' and 'ERC', found none of those terms anywhere on the page, so that portion of the claim is removed; only the April-2026-freeze portion of the same evidence item, which the page does support, is retained. Both named listed vehicles being non-committed, plus an open-ended regulatory freeze with no sourced resolution date, together argue for a score below the 'credible inside the window' anchor rather than at it. Not scored lower still: Gulf and WHA are both real, named companies actively planning within a three-to-five-year frame that sits inside the 2-5 year horizon, and the freeze is evidenced as a pause tied to a specific new rule rather than a cancellation.

notes.text: anchor_date is derived, not copied: the candidate's campaign_record.occurrence carries source_name/source_date/url but no formal {kind, anchor_date, window} block in the method section 0 shape, because that shape is written for signals, not candidates. The occurrence is UNDERWAY (a structural build-out with an in-progress regulatory response), so per method section 0 snapping (quarter/half to midpoint) the anchor is set to the midpoint of the quantified Q1 2026 BOI reporting period, 2026-02-15. Window: Q1 2026 BOI investment-application surge (reported 2026-04-29) through the mid-2026 grid-capacity rule (Royal Gazette 2026-06-05) and the resulting application pause, ongoing as of 2026-08-29 (SCMP) and 2026-08-22 (The Star).

LEAKY here is not the Arctic case's 'the beneficiaries are sanctioned and unlisted.' It is the more common leaky shape: two large, real, listed direct plays exist (Gulf, WHA) inside a much larger pool whose residual is not attributable to any specific listed name on the sourcing this run could open, plus a live regulatory shock (the grid-confirmation rule) that has already paused new promotion filings since April 2026. A chain build here should start from the Gulf/WHA power-and-land layer rather than from the BOI headline total, and should treat both the application pause and Gulf's own capex figure being an unconverted ceiling as live timing risks, not one-off caveats.
